chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, raising it to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
If a man dies on a ship and it is not possible to reach the shore, he said: “He is shrouded, camphor is applied to him in a cloth, and he is cast into the water.”

key_terms.السَّفِينَةِ: the ship or vessel in which the death occurs
key_terms.الشَّطِّ: the shore or riverbank/land that cannot be reached
key_terms.الْمَاءِ: the water into which the deceased is placed
key_terms.ثَوْبٍ: a cloth used for covering or shrouding
key_terms.يُحَنَّطُ: camphor or burial perfume is applied to him
key_terms.يُكَفَّنُ: he is wrapped in a burial shroud

ai.seo_question: What should be done if a person dies on a ship and the shore cannot be reached?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling for handling the dead when someone dies aboard a ship and reaching land is not possible. It instructs that the deceased be shrouded and prepared with hanut, then consigned to the water.
